response.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune
  FROM orderexecutions e
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark
),
counts AS (
  SELECT ordertune, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY ordertune
),
shares AS (
  SELECT ordertune, cnt,
         CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share
  FROM counts
),
avgs AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares
)
SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count,
       AVG(s.share) AS avg_share,
       AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess
FROM shares s
CROSS JOIN avgs a
WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Executions are linked to orders with an inner join on orderexecutions.ordersmark = orders.recordvault, so executions without a matching order are dropped.

Each order type's count is the number of joined execution rows, so an order with several executions contributes once per execution. Orders with a NULL ordertune form their own group, which GROUP BY keeps as a single NULL group and which is included in the average share.
Each type's share is its count divided by the total count across all types. The overall average share is the unweighted mean of those per-type shares.

The 'average amount by which their share exceeds the overall average' is the mean of (share minus overall average share) over the qualifying types. Output is unrounded. If no type qualifies, total_count is NULL.
